chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who joins the end of the Imam's prayer, while it is the beginning of the man's prayer, so he does not wait for the Imam to finish recitation, but completes the recitation in the last part of his own prayer. He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.آخِرُ صَلاَةِ الْإِمَامِ: The end of the Imam's prayer (from the follower's perspective of joining)
key_terms.آخِرِ صَلاَتِهِ: The end of his (the follower's) prayer
key_terms.أَوَّلُ صَلاَةِ الرَّجُلِ: The beginning of the follower's prayer

ai.seo_question: How should a worshipper recite the Quran if they join the Imam after the Imam has already started reciting?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural mechanics of joining a congregational prayer late, specifically addressing the synchronization of the follower's individual recitation with the Imam's ongoing recitation. It establishes that the follower is not required to remain silent until the Imam concludes his recitation but may instead perform their own *Al-Fatiha* concurrently, completing it as the Imam proceeds to bowing or other actions. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of individual acts within the communal framework when timing constraints arise.
